title: The backlog check runs at its CPU limit on CI, so a busy runner fails a pull request whose tests all pass

source.ref: #5044 on 2026-11-16: the full sweep burned 440.0 s of CPU against a 437.8 s budget with every probe passing.

detail: MEASURED 2026-11-16 on the 4-core cloud box, full sweep (--probes=all), main at 771c0ef80: 2,424 costed probes, 291 to 313 s of guard CPU across five runs, so run-to-run noise alone is about 7% while CI had 0.5% of headroom. WHERE THE TIME GOES: an empty node start costs 25 ms and 1,801 probes cost under 40 ms each (47 s together). 240 probes cost over 300 ms each and burn 201 s of 291 s (69%): 47 are over 1 s (89 s) and 193 are 300 ms to 1 s (112 s). They are the probes that start a test runner or a heavy script (SCAN-502 10.5 s, LIVE-2273 4.5 s, BLD-203 3.9 s, BLD-202 3.5 s, BLD-205 3.4 s; BLD-203 runs npx vitest on one file). This is cost spread across many probes, which the per-probe ceiling (6.5 s) is not built to see; the count-scaled total is the only assertion that does. Unexplained: this box reads about 300 s where CI read 440 s for the same sweep, so the CI figure needs its own per-probe dump before anything is retimed. RULED OUT: lane count. 2, 4 and 8 probes in flight cost 316, 303 and 297 to 313 s, so oversubscription is not what inflates the reading. SHIPPED WITH THIS ROW: one V8 compile cache shared by every probe in a sweep (NODE_COMPILE_CACHE, a temp directory removed on exit), which measured 276 to 292 s over six runs (mean 281 against 302 without), about 7% less. That is headroom, not the fix. WHAT CLOSES IT, either or both: (1) convert the 47 probes over 1 s to measure their consequence in-process instead of spawning a suite (the LIVE-034 pattern), which needs the owner's phrase per probe because it rewrites probes; (2) make the budget immune to runner speed by timing a fixed reference workload in the same run and asserting the ratio, which rewrites a test pin and also needs the owner's phrase. Do not raise BASE_CPU_MS or PER_PROBE_ALLOWANCE_MS without a paired CI and local reading (ADR-1107). UPDATE 2026-11-16 (owner picked A: make the budget relative to runner speed). The guard now prints runner-speed (one fixed piece of work per 100 probes, same lanes). Paired reading: CI checks job 73.2 ms, local box 82.6 to 87.3 ms. The same full sweep read 265.2 s on #5064's test job and 440.0 s on #5044's, a 1.66x spread on an unchanged list, so the spread is the runner. The contract test now multiplies the count-scaled total by runner-speed over a 75 ms reference, never below 1 and capped at 2.5, and fails if the runner-speed line goes missing. The per-probe ceiling (6.5 s) is NOT scaled and SCAN-502 read 10 to 20 s on the loaded local box against 3.7 s on CI: that ceiling is the next thing a slow runner trips, and it needs its own reading before it is touched. Still open: the 47 probes over 1 s. CARRIED OVER FROM HYG-243 (parked as a duplicate of this row): on #5044 the guard total was 32.7 s above what the probes reported (440.0 s against 407.3 s), far more than the 2 s base assumes; on #5064 the gap was 28.6 s (265.2 against 236.6). Nobody has attributed that CPU yet. It is work the per-probe report does not see, most likely shells and non-node children of probes. Attribute it before converting probes. ATTRIBUTED 2026-11-16 (the HYG-243 carry-over): full sweep on the 4-core box, n=2430 probes, 8 in flight. The guard process reaped 280.6 s of child CPU while the probes reported 262.8 s and the reference work 2.2 s, so 15.6 s of child CPU was never reported; the guard itself used 5.1 s (3.3 user, 1.8 system). Total 285.8 s against the 270.1 s the guard-cost line prints, a 23 s gap, the same shape as CI 28.6 and 32.7 s on a runner about 1.3 to 1.7x slower. Where the 15.6 s goes, measured on 200 spawns of a bare node -e 0 with the preload: 4.2 ms per probe is reaped but not reported when spawned through the shell, 2.7 ms when spawned directly. So about 2.7 ms is node teardown after the preload exit hook writes its line, and about 1.5 ms is the sh -c wrapper; times 2455 spawns that is about 10 s, the rest being longer teardown in the heavy probes. CONCLUSION: the gap is per-spawn process overhead that grows with the probe count, not hidden work, and the 180 ms per-probe allowance already covers it. Dropping the shell would save about 4 s (1.3%) and change how every probe string is parsed, so it is not worth doing. The next step remains converting the 47 probes over 1 s, which needs the owner phrase per probe. BLD-203 SPLIT 2026-11-16 (owner approval on the decision card, 20:31 UTC): main's test job read BLD-203 at 6468 ms against the 6.5 s per-probe ceiling (run 43946371883, 99.5 percent, unscaled by runner speed). Its test file imported the whole editor block config (about 2 s of import) for the Tune rail case and the role renders. The render half now reads the role blocks from components/page-editor/blocks/roles, and the Tune rail case plus a check that the editor config serves those same role blocks moved to lib/builder/variants-tune.test.ts, which pnpm test runs. Local probe CPU went from 3.95 to 4.15 s down to 2.81 to 3.03 s (about 28 percent), so CI should read about 4.6 s, about 70 percent of the ceiling. The probe file itself is unchanged. LIVE-2273 SPEEDUP 2026-11-16: its probe (node scripts/check-adoption.mjs, shared by 9 rows) read 6.54 s CPU on #5141 against the 6.5 s ceiling. The gate recompiled every scope glob per file and built a per-character array of every file to blank comments. Globs are now compiled once and comments are blanked from slices; output is byte-identical (all 9,340 files compared) and local CPU went from about 4.2 s to 2.1 s. No probe or test edit. 2026-11-18 PROBE REWRITES (owner approval, Daniel, project thread 17:52Z, answer 1. A: "rewrite the slowest checks to run in-process"). Thirteen probes that spawned a second vitest run now ask, in-process, that their test files are still in the required test job's run with their cases (scripts/probes/in-suite.mjs, the SCAN-1176 / LIVE-034 pattern): BLD-202, BLD-203, BLD-204, BLD-205, FH-007, LIVE-2275, LIVE-2297, LIVE-2298, LIVE-2299, LIVE-2300, LIVE-2304, LIVE-2305, HYG-226. Each keeps its source checks; a test file that goes missing, is excluded by vitest.config.ts, drops below the case count it has today, or carries .skip/.only/.todo turns its row back to OPEN. pnpm test still runs every one of those files on every pull request. Local full sweep on the 4-core box with two other agents running: guardCpuMs 303.7 s before, 266.8 s after (12 percent less); BLD-205 (7.0 s), BLD-202 (6.6 s) and BLD-203 (4.1 s) leave the slowest list, which now starts SCAN-502 (dead-exports, 8.8 s here, under the ceiling in CI) and the PROG-E6 in-process probes at about 2 s. CI readings on main before this change (test job, unscaled budget 2000 + 180 x 2527 = 456.9 s): 294.0, 363.5, 418.1, 421.8, 274.9 s. Row stays open until its own probe reads ten checks runs at or under 85 percent; BASE_CPU_MS and PER_PROBE_ALLOWANCE_MS are unchanged.

verify.evidence: Fails today: #5044's checks run printed guardCpuMs 440.0 s against a 437.8 s budget. Passes when ten checks runs in a row on main print a guard-cost line at or under 85% of the budget the contract test computes for that probe count.
